studies.population: Adults undergoing elective laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia
studies.key_findings: Drug A significantly reduced PONV incidence at 24h; adverse events were infrequent and similar between arms.
studies.notes: This trial was independently indexed by both openalex (native id W1001) and crossref (native id C2001), sharing DOI 10.1111/aaa -- tools/dedup.py's exact pass merges them by DOI, and canonicalizes to whichever source's raw file sorts first lexicographically ('crossref-*' before 'openalex-*'), so crossref:C2001 is this study's canonical record_id, not openalex:W1001.

reports.citation: Kim JH, Lee SY. (2022). Effect of Drug A on postoperative nausea and vomiting: a randomized controlled trial. Journal of Anesthesia, 36(4), 512-520.

source.quote: PONV occurred in 10 of 60 (16.7%) patients in the Drug A group versus 25 of 60 (41.7%) in the placebo group.
Adverse events occurred in 3 patients in the Drug A group and 2 in the placebo group, all mild.

allocation_concealment.support: Sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes, Methods 2.2.

blinding_outcome_assessment.support: Outcome assessors blinded to group assignment, Methods 2.4.

incomplete_outcome_data.support: 2/60 (3.3%) lost to follow-up, balanced across arms.

selective_reporting.support: Prespecified outcomes in registered protocol (NCT-AAA) all reported.

studies.population: Adults undergoing elective gynecologic surgery under general anesthesia
studies.key_findings: Drug B significantly reduced PONV incidence at 24h.

reports.citation: Park JY. (2021). Randomized trial of Drug B for prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting. Anesthesia & Analgesia, 133(2), 401-408.

source.quote: PONV occurred in 8 of 55 (14.5%) patients receiving Drug B versus 20 of 55 (36.4%) receiving placebo.

incomplete_outcome_data.support: 12/55 (21.8%) lost to follow-up in the intervention arm versus 2/55 (3.6%) in placebo, unbalanced and unexplained.

selective_reporting.support: No trial registry found, but all outcomes described in Methods were reported.

studies.population: Adults undergoing elective orthopedic surgery under general anesthesia
studies.key_findings: Drug C reduced PONV incidence and postoperative pain scores at 24h.
studies.notes: risk_of_bias.tool was originally recorded as the legacy 'RoB2' label for this framework's RoB1 six-domain tool -- kept as-is to exercise normalize_risk_of_bias's legacy-alias handling.

reports.citation: Choi HJ. (2020). Pain outcomes after Drug C: a randomized controlled trial. Pain Medicine, 21(9), 1801-1809.

source.quote: PONV occurred in 15 of 65 (23.1%) patients in the Drug C group versus 22 of 65 (33.8%) in the placebo group.
Mean pain score (0-10 NRS) at 24h was 3.2 (SD 1.1) in the Drug C group and 4.0 (SD 1.3) in the placebo group.

incomplete_outcome_data.support: 3/65 (4.6%) lost to follow-up, balanced across arms.

selective_reporting.support: No trial registry entry found or cited.

studies.population: Adults undergoing elective abdominal surgery under general anesthesia
studies.intervention: Intravenous Drug D 5mg at induction (per surgeon's discretion)
studies.key_findings: Drug D was associated with lower postoperative pain scores at 24h in this cohort.

reports.citation: Jung MK. (2019). Cohort study of Drug D and postoperative pain. Journal of Clinical Anesthesia, 55, 88-94.

source.quote: Mean pain score (0-10 NRS) at 24h was 3.5 (SD 1.0) in the Drug D group and 4.2 (SD 1.2) in the comparison group.

selection.support: Representativeness of exposed cohort, selection of non-exposed cohort, and ascertainment of exposure all described (Methods 2.1-2.3); outcome-not-present-at-baseline not explicitly confirmed.

comparability.support: Adjusted for surgical duration (Methods 2.5); no adjustment for baseline pain or opioid use.

outcome.support: Outcome assessment and adequacy of follow-up described (Methods 2.6); follow-up duration not explicitly justified as sufficient.
